newsitem.title: USA: Abbott buying French maker of analyzers.
newsitem.headline: Abbott buying French maker of analyzers.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc said Friday it is buying Alcyon Analyzer SA, a French manufacturer of low-volume, benchtop clinical chemistry analyzers.
Abbott said it will obtain 100 percent of the shares of privately held Alycon. Specific financial terms were not disclosed.
Alycon, based in Saint Mathieu de Treviers, France, makes and sells a family of three low-volume, clinical chemistry instruments.

"This acquisition represents an excellent opportunity for Abbott to quickly establish a presence in low-volume clinical chemistry throughout the world," Miles White, senior vice president, diagnostic operations, said in a statement. "Alcyon's family of analyzers allows Abbott to compete against older product offerings in the benchtop chemistry segment. Additionally, with Abbott's sales presence in fast-growing emerging markets, and in alternate sites in the United States, the Alcyon analyzers position us well for future growth."
Clinical chemistry comprises dozens of tests, including tests for glucose, electrolytes, enzymes, protein and lipids, which are measured as overall indicators of human health, Abbott said.
Abbott said the worldwide market for clinical chemistry is estimated to be $3.7 billion, with growth rates of one to two percent.

The low-volume segment accounts for over $500 million. The majority of sales for this segment are in developing countries and are growing at one to three percent a year, Abbott said. But emerging markets are growing at annual rates of 11 to 13 percent for low-volume clinical chemistry, it added.
